response:
{
  "headline": "VISTA-16 phase 3 trial of varespladib stopped early for futility; human genetics show PLA2G2A has no causal role in coronary disease (association score 0.0), making target_not_causal the primary failure mode.",
  "summary": "The VISTA-16 trial randomized 5,189–6,500 acute coronary syndrome patients to varespladib or placebo on top of atorvastatin 80 mg daily, with a primary morbidity/mortality endpoint at 16 weeks. The independent DSMB recommended stopping the study on 9 March 2012 due to lack of efficacy, and enrollment was closed with patients removed from therapy. Human genetic evidence gives PLA2G2A a coronary artery disorder association score of 0.0 with zero evidence items, indicating no causal link, and the intended biomarker sPLA2-IIA mass is classified as non-causal. The phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS trial had already shown varespladib reduced LDL-C and inflammatory biomarkers by ~84–87% but produced no difference in clinical cardiovascular events. Confidence in the target_not_causal conclusion is high.",
  "key_evidence": [
    "Genetic association score for PLA2G2A with coronary artery disorder: 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G2A)",
    "Trial stopped early for futility per DSMB recommendation on 9 March 2012 (Anthera Halts VISTA-16 Clinical Study Due to Lack of Efficacy Following Recommendation by the Independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (PRNewswire, 9 March 2012))",
    "Patients randomized: 5,189 participants (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01130246 VISTA-16) or 6,500 patients (Varespladib)",
    "Placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction only -6.2% (drug -49.6% vs placebo -43.4% at 8 weeks on atorvastatin background) (Effects of varespladib methyl on biomarkers and major cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome patients; Anti-inflammatory effects of varespladib methyl in diabetic patients with acute coronary syndrome)",
    "sPLA2-IIA reduced -83.6% within-arm at 500 mg daily, 8 weeks (Anti-inflammatory effects of varespladib methyl in diabetic patients with acute coronary syndrome)",
    "Calculator expected HR 0.97 (3% RRR) from placebo-adjusted LDL-C change; would require ~33,076 events for 80% power (calculator)",
    "Phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS showed no treatment differences in clinical cardiovascular events (Effects of varespladib methyl on biomarkers and major cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome patients)",
    "Primary endpoint: morbidity and mortality at 16 weeks (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01130246 VISTA-16)"
  ],
  "what_would_change_this": "Nothing — the conclusion is already settled by human genetics showing PLA2G2A has no causal role in coronary disease (association score 0.0); additional trial data would not change this.",
  "readthrough_note": "No read-through programmes identified; the read-through list is empty."
}
